title: sieve-native: RFC 5229 variables extension
description:
Add the variables extension (RFC 5229). Because the evaluator already dispatches on Word(name), variables integrate as two small additions with no structural changes.

What: additions to evaluator.rs only. No parser changes needed.

The form reader already produces Str(s) for all quoted strings. Variable substitution is a post-read pass on string values before use, not a parser concern.

Addition 1 — expand_str():
  fn expand_str(s: &str, vars: &HashMap<String,String>) -> String
  Scan for ${name} patterns; replace with vars.get(name).unwrap_or("").
  Variable names are case-insensitive: normalize to lowercase on lookup.
  Call this on every Str(s) value before passing to comparators or actions.
  If require ["variables"] not declared, expand_str is a no-op (returns s unchanged).

Addition 2 — eval_set():
  match rest { [Modifier*, Str(name), Str(value)] => ... }
  Modifiers are Form::Tag values: lower, upper, length, quotewildcard, firstline.
  Apply in order:
    lower        → ASCII lowercase the expanded value
    upper        → ASCII uppercase
    length       → replace with decimal string of char count
    quotewildcard → escape * and ? with \
    firstline    → truncate at first \n (or \r\n)
  ctx.vars.insert(name.to_lowercase(), result)

Addition 3 — require check:
  compile() already validates require declarations. Add "variables" to the known extensions list.
  Any script using ${...} or set without require ["variables"] → compile error.

That is the entire variables implementation. No other files change. The form-based architecture makes this additive.
